summary: Defines how to send multiple attachments in one EDIINT message. EDIINT AS1, AS2, and AS3 were designed for transporting EDI documents, but later uses needed several attachments per transaction. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Businesses send electronic forms to each other. This lets them attach several files to one message, like putting more than one paper in the same envelope.

questions: how to send multiple attachments with ediint
subtitle: How to send multiple documents in a single business message.

tldr.problem: EDIINT AS1, AS2, and AS3 were designed to send one EDI document per message, but businesses sometimes need to send multiple related documents in a single message.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes using the MIME multipart/related structure to wrap multiple attachments of any type within one EDIINT message, and explains how to calculate message integrity checks across the entire multipart body.
tldr.outcome: Organizations can now send several documents (XML, PDF, Word, images, etc.) together in a single transaction while preserving message integrity.

facts.label: Supported MIME types
facts.value: At least 12 types including XML, PDF, Word, RTF, ZIP, images, plain text, and HTML

today: RFC 6362 is an Informational RFC that extends EDIINT capability. It has not been obsoleted and remains the specification for sending multiple attachments in EDIINT messages. Organizations adopting EDIINT for multi-document transactions use this approach.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
EDIINT (Electronic Data Interchange - Internet Integration) includes three protocols: AS1 over SMTP, AS2 over HTTP, and AS3 over FTP. They were originally designed to securely transport EDI documents over the Internet. As EDIINT adoption grew beyond pure EDI, new uses emerged where a single business transaction required multiple documents together in one message.

This RFC describes how to attach and transmit multiple documents (including non-EDI files) in a single EDIINT message using the MIME multipart/related structure.
sections.plainLanguage: Electronic forms get sent between businesses. Sometimes you need to attach more than one file to one delivery, like attaching several papers to one email instead of separate emails.

sections.title: The Multipart/Related Structure
sections.content:
Multiple attachments in EDIINT are stored in a MIME multipart/related body as defined in RFC 2387. This structure allows several documents to be communicated in a single message. The type parameter identifies the root document type, and the optional start parameter can specify which attachment is the main one. A MIME type can be any agreed-upon type: application/xml, application/pdf, application/msword, text/plain, image/jpeg, and so on.

The RFC specifies a minimum list of MIME types that must be supported: XML, PDF, Word, RTF, ZIP archives, GIF/TIFF/JPEG images, plain text, HTML, and raw bytes.
sections.plainLanguage: The multipart structure is like a container that holds several different file types together. You label which file is the main one and what types of files are inside.

sections.title: Features and Integrity
sections.content:
EDIINT applications that support multiple attachments must announce this capability with the EDIINT-Features: multiple-attachments header in every message.

Message integrity checking (MIC) is calculated over the entire multipart/related body rather than a single EDI payload. For encrypted or compressed messages, the MIC is computed over the uncompressed, decrypted multipart body. For unsigned and unencrypted messages, the MIC is calculated over the data inside the multipart boundaries prior to any Content-Transfer-Encoding. If the calculated MIC differs from the expected MIC, all attachments are considered invalid and must be retransmitted.
sections.plainLanguage: The message has a check code to detect if anything got scrambled in transit. The check code covers all the files together, not just one file. If the check fails, everything is retransmitted.

sections.title: Document Processing and Examples
sections.content:
Upon receipt, the receiving application must extract the individual attachments from the multipart/related body rather than simply removing the multipart wrapper. The storing and processing of the documents is implementation dependent and must follow any trading-partner agreements.

For example, an AS2 message can wrap two attachments: an XML document as the root and a PDF document as a second attachment. Both are signed as part of the overall message structure. The multipart/related structure is nested within a signed outer structure so that the entire set of attachments is protected by the digital signature.
sections.plainLanguage: When the message arrives, you pull out each separate file instead of just removing a wrapper. How you store and use them depends on your specific setup.
